s: Romansh for 'high peak', 3,246m above St Moritz
w: Piz Ot takes its name from the Romansh for "high peak" and, at 3,246m, is the high point of the range lying north of Pass Suvretta. The standard route to the summit starts from the heights of St Moritz and Samedan, climbing the mountain's southern side.
_facts: 3,246m mountain of the Albula Alps, west of Samedan, Graubunden
Name is Romansh for 'high peak'
Culminating point of the range north of Pass Suvretta
Normal route starts from the heights of St Moritz and Samedan

s: 3,165m summit above Lake Sils and the Julier Pass
w: Piz Lagrev rises 3,165m over Lake Sils, the high point of the ridge between the Septimer and Julier passes. The Julier road runs right beneath its northern flank, and a small glacier, the Vadret Lagrev, feeds an unnamed lake at the mountain's foot.
_facts: 3,165m mountain of the Albula Alps overlooking Lake Sils, Graubunden
Culminating point of the range between the Septimer Pass and Julier Pass
Julier Pass lies on its northern side
Glacier Vadret Lagrev and an unnamed lake lie on its northeast side

s: 4,048m: the highest peak in the Eastern Alps
w: At 4,048m, Piz Bernina is the highest peak in the Eastern Alps and the only Alpine four-thousander lying entirely within Switzerland. Johann Coaz named it after the Bernina Pass in 1850, the year he made its first ascent. The summit, near St Moritz, is ringed by glaciers, chief among them the Morteratsch.
_facts: Highest mountain in the Eastern Alps at 4,048m, highest point of the canton of Grisons
Named after the Bernina Pass in 1850 by Johann Coaz, who made the first ascent
Entirely surrounded by glaciers, the largest being the Morteratsch Glacier
Summit lies in Switzerland; the massif straddles the border with Italy

w: Walking the woods beside Lake Silvaplana in August 1881, Friedrich Nietzsche conceived his idea of Eternal Recurrence, as he later recounted in Ecce Homo. The lake now draws kitesurfers each summer and, once frozen, the Engadin Skimarathon and snowkiters in winter, framed by Piz Corvatsch and Piz Julier.
_facts: Lake in the Upper Engadine valley, among the largest lakes in Grisons alongside Lake Sils
Nietzsche conceived the idea of Eternal Recurrence walking here in August 1881, per Ecce Homo
Used for kitesurfing and windsurfing in summer; the Engadin Skimarathon crosses it once frozen
Overlooked by Piz Corvatsch, Piz Julier and Piz Surlej

s: 2,312m pass with a hospice and a cyclist's memorial
w: The Albula Pass carries a paved road and, lower down through the Albula Tunnel, the Rhaetian Railway, over its 2,312m summit, where a hospice still stands. In June 2025 a memorial sculpture, Connected, was unveiled here for cyclist Gino Mader, who died descending the pass during the 2023 Tour de Suisse.
_facts: 2,312m mountain pass in Graubunden linking central Grisons with the Engadin
Crossed by a paved road via Bergun and by the Rhaetian Railway through the Albula Tunnel
A hospice stands at the summit; the lake Albulasee lies just east of the pass
A 2025 memorial sculpture, Connected, honours cyclist Gino Mader, who died here in the 2023 Tour de Suisse

s: Cable car to 3,298m over two Engadin lakes
w: A cable car climbs from Surlej to 3,298m on Piz Corvatsch, among the highest lift-served points in the Eastern Alps, leaving only a short traverse over Piz Murtel to the 3,451m true summit. Glaciers cling to its eastern face above Lake Sils and Lake Silvaplana, anchoring one of Switzerland's highest ski areas.
_facts: 3,451m mountain in the Bernina Range overlooking Lake Sils and Lake Silvaplana
Cable car runs from Surlej to an upper station at 3,298m
Massif also includes Piz Murtel (3,433m); glaciers Vadret dal Murtel and Vadret dal Corvatsch lie on its east side
Part of one of the highest ski areas in Switzerland and the Eastern Alps

w: First climbed on 11 September 1858 by C. Brugger and P. Gensler with local guides, Piz Morteratsch rises 3,751m between the Morteratsch and Tschierva glaciers. Its harder ridges drew Victorian mountaineers, among them the husband-and-wife pair T. H. Philpott and Mrs Philpott, who took the southwest ridge in 1868.
_facts: 3,751m mountain in the Bernina Range, bordered by the Morteratsch and Tschierva glaciers
First ascent 11 September 1858 by C. Brugger and P. Gensler with guides Karl Emmermann and Angelo Klaingutti
Southwest ridge first climbed in 1868 by T. H. Philpott and Mrs Philpott with guides
Served by the Boval hut (2,495m) and Tschierva Hut (2,573m)

s: Summit of the famous Biancograt snow ridge
w: Also called Piz Alv, Piz Bianco tops out at 3,993m as the high point of the Biancograt, a narrow snow arete rated among the most beautiful ridge routes in the Alps. Climbers bound for the higher Piz Bernina just south of it traverse this summit on the way, tracing the ridge's icy crest.
_facts: 3,993m minor summit north of Piz Bernina, also known as Piz Alv
Highest point of the Biancograt ridge (also called Crast'Alva)
Located south of Pontresina in Graubunden
Often traversed by climbers heading for Piz Bernina

s: Via ferrata to 3,380m over the Julier Pass
w: A via ferrata called the Senda Enferrada climbs the final stretch to Piz Julier's 3,380m summit, reached via the Fuorcla Albana pass at 2,870m on a trail out of St Moritz. It is the second-highest peak in the range between the Julier and Albula passes, standing directly over the Julier road below.
_facts: 3,380m mountain of the Albula Alps overlooking the Julier Pass
Second-highest peak, after Piz Calderas, between the Julier and Albula passes
Trail from St Moritz leads to Fuorcla Albana (2,870m)
Via ferrata Senda Enferrada continues to the summit

s: Funicular to a panoramic restaurant over Engadin
w: A funicular, the Muottas-Muragl-Bahn, hauls visitors from Rhaetian Railway stations at Punt Muragl up to 2,454m, where a hotel and panoramic restaurant look out over the whole Engadin - St Moritz, Samedan and Pontresina laid out below in a single sweep of valley.
_facts: 2,454m viewpoint on the southern slopes of the Blais da Muottas, Samedan municipality
Reached by the Muottas-Muragl-Bahn funicular between Celerina and Pontresina
Served by the Punt Muragl and Punt Muragl Staz stations on the Rhaetian Railway
Includes a hotel and panoramic restaurant overlooking Samedan, St Moritz and Pontresina

w: Piz da la Margna has drawn climbers since June 1857, when J. Caviezel and three companions made its first recorded tourist ascent. The 3,158m peak overlooks Lake Sils southeast of the Maloja Pass; its harder southeast ridge went unclimbed until 1918, when Hans Frick and two partners finally took it.
_facts: 3,158m mountain in the Bernina Range overlooking Lake Sils, southeast of the Maloja Pass
First recorded tourist ascent June 1857 by J. Caviezel, Krattli, Robbi and Zaun
Southeast ridge first climbed 14 August 1918 by Hans Frick, Christian Zippert and Hans Casper

s: Trail from Diavolezza over Morteratsch Glacier
w: Munt Pers looks straight down onto the Morteratsch Glacier from just north of Diavolezza, whose cable car delivers walkers to a trail climbing on to the summit - one of the most direct close-up views of the ice fields spilling from Piz Bernina.
_facts: Mountain in the Bernina Range overlooking the Morteratsch Glacier
Lies just north of Diavolezza
A trail leads from Diavolezza to its summit
